passages.text: Once again Jesus began to teach beside the sea, and such a large crowd gathered around Him that He got into a boat and sat in it, while all the people crowded along the shore.
passages.sermon:
Jesus began to teach again.
He taught beside the sea.
A very large crowd gathered around Jesus.
The crowd was so large that Jesus got into a boat.
Jesus sat in the boat on the sea.
All the people stayed on the shore.
The people crowded along the land by the sea.
passages.original: Καὶ πάλιν ἤρξατο διδάσκειν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ συνάγεται πρὸς αὐτὸν ὄχλος πλεῖστος ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς πλοῖον ἐμβάντα καθῆσθαι ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος πρὸς τὴν θάλασσαν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἦσαν

passages.text: And He taught them many things in parables, and in His teaching He said, “Listen! A farmer went out to sow his seed.
passages.sermon:
Jesus taught the people many things.
He used parables to teach them.
He spoke to them during His teaching.
He said, “Listen.
A farmer went out to sow his seed.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς ἐν παραβολαῖς πολλά καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ἐν τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ Ἀκούετε ἰδοὺ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρων σπεῖραι

passages.text: And as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured it.
passages.sermon:
Jesus taught a large crowd by the sea.
He spoke to them using parables.
He told them about a farmer who went out to sow seed.
As the farmer sowed, some seed fell along the path.
Birds came to the path.
The birds ate the seed that fell there.
passages.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ σπείρειν ὃ μὲν ἔπεσεν παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν καὶ ἦλθεν τὰ πετεινὰ καὶ κατέφαγεν αὐτό

passages.text: Some fell on rocky ground, where it did not have much soil. It sprang up quickly because the soil was shallow.
passages.sermon:
Jesus taught the people using parables.
He told them about a farmer who went out to sow seed.
Some seed fell on rocky ground.
This ground did not have much soil.
The seed sprang up quickly.
The soil was shallow.
passages.original: Καὶ ἄλλο ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὸ πετρῶδες ὅπου οὐκ εἶχεν γῆν πολλήν καὶ εὐθὺς ἐξανέτειλεν διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν βάθος γῆς

passages.text: But when the sun rose, the seedlings were scorched, and they withered because they had no root.
passages.sermon:
The sun rose.
The seedlings stood in the sunlight.
The sun scorched the seedlings.
The seedlings had no root.
The seedlings withered.
passages.original: καὶ ὅτε ἀνέτειλεν ὁ ἥλιος ἐκαυματίσθη καὶ διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ῥίζαν ἐξηράνθη

passages.text: Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up and choked the seedlings, and they yielded no crop.
passages.sermon:
Some seed fell among thorns.
The thorns grew up.
The thorns choked the seed.
The seed did not produce any crop.
passages.original: Καὶ ἄλλο ἔπεσεν εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας καὶ ἀνέβησαν αἱ ἄκανθαι καὶ συνέπνιξαν αὐτό καὶ καρπὸν οὐκ ἔδωκεν

passages.text: Still other seed fell on good soil, where it sprouted, grew up, and produced a crop—one bearing thirtyfold, another sixtyfold, and another a hundredfold.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus told a parable about a sower.
Some seed fell on good soil.
This seed sprouted.
It grew up.
It produced a crop.
Some plants yielded thirty times what was sown.
Some plants yielded sixty times what was sown.
Some plants yielded a hundred times what was sown.
passages.original: Καὶ ἄλλα ἔπεσεν εἰς τὴν γῆν τὴν καλήν καὶ ἐδίδου καρπὸν ἀναβαίνοντα καὶ αὐξανόμενα καὶ ἔφερεν ἓν τριάκοντα καὶ ἓν ἑξήκοντα καὶ ἓν ἑκατόν

passages.text: Then Jesus said, “He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the people.\r\nJesus said, “If anyone has ears, he should listen.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν Ὃς ἔχει ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω

passages.text: As soon as Jesus was alone with the Twelve and those around Him, they asked Him about the parable.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was with the Twelve disciples.
Other people were also with Jesus.
They were alone together.
These people asked Jesus about the parable.
passages.original: Καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο κατὰ μόνας ἠρώτων αὐτὸν οἱ περὶ αὐτὸν σὺν τοῖς δώδεκα τὰς παραβολάς

passages.text: He replied, “The mystery of the kingdom of God has been given to you, but to those on the outside everything is expressed in parables, so that, ‘they may be ever seeing but never perceiving, and ever hearing but never understanding; otherwise they might turn and be forgiven.’”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples and those with Him.
He said, “God has given you the mystery of His kingdom.
You understand this secret.
But people outside do not receive it directly.
I speak to them using parables.
They see, but they do not truly see.
They hear, but they do not truly understand.
If they understood, they might turn to God.
Then God would forgive them.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Ὑμῖν τὸ μυστήριον δέδοται τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐκείνοις δὲ τοῖς ἔξω ἐν παραβολαῖς τὰ πάντα γίνεται ἵνα Βλέποντες βλέπωσιν καὶ μὴ ἴδωσιν Καὶ ἀκούοντες ἀκούωσιν καὶ μὴ συνιῶσιν Μή‿ ποτε ἐπιστρέψωσιν Καὶ ἀφεθῇ αὐτοῖς

passages.text: Then Jesus said to them, “Do you not understand this parable? Then how will you understand any of the parables?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus asked them a question.
He said, “You do not understand this parable.
If you do not understand this parable, you will not understand any parable.”
passages.original: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Οὐκ οἴδατε τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην καὶ πῶς πάσας τὰς παραβολὰς γνώσεσθε

passages.text: The farmer sows the word.
passages.sermon: A farmer sows seeds.\r\nThe seeds represent the word of God.\r\nThe farmer spreads the word of God.
passages.original: Ὁ σπείρων τὸν λόγον σπείρει

passages.text: Some are like the seeds along the path, where the word is sown. As soon as they hear it, Satan comes and takes away the word that was sown in them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He explained the meaning of the parable.
Some people are like seeds sown along the path.
The word of God is sown in them.
They hear the word.
Immediately, Satan comes.
Satan takes away the word that was sown in them.
passages.original: οὗτοι δέ εἰσιν οἱ παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ὅπου σπείρεται ὁ λόγος καὶ ὅταν ἀκούσωσιν εὐθὺς ἔρχεται ὁ Σατανᾶς καὶ αἴρει τὸν λόγον τὸν ἐσπαρμένον εἰς αὐτούς

passages.text: Some are like the seeds sown on rocky ground. They hear the word and at once receive it with joy.
passages.sermon:
Some people are like seeds sown on rocky ground.
These people hear the word.
They receive the word at once.
They receive it with joy.
passages.original: Καὶ οὗτοί εἰσιν ὁμοίως οἱ ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη σπειρόμενοι οἳ ὅταν ἀκούσωσιν τὸν λόγον εὐθὺς μετὰ χαρᾶς λαμβάνουσιν αὐτόν

passages.text: But they themselves have no root, and they remain for only a season. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they quickly fall away.
passages.sermon:
These people are like seeds sown on rocky ground.
They hear the word and receive it with joy.
They do not have root in themselves.
They last only for a short time.
Trouble or persecution comes because of the word.
They quickly fall away.
passages.original: καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν ῥίζαν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἀλλὰ πρόσκαιροί εἰσιν εἶτα γενομένης θλίψεως ἢ διωγμοῦ διὰ τὸν λόγον εὐθὺς σκανδαλίζονται

passages.text: Others are like the seeds sown among the thorns. They hear the word, but the worries of this life, the deceitfulness of wealth, and the desire for other things come in and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
passages.sermon:
Some people are like seeds sown among thorns.
These people hear the word.
The worries of this life come in.
The deceitfulness of wealth comes in.
The desire for other things comes in.
These things choke the word.
The word becomes unfruitful in them.
passages.original: Καὶ ἄλλοι εἰσὶν οἱ εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας σπειρόμενοι οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ τὸν λόγον ἀκούσαντες καὶ αἱ μέριμναι τοῦ αἰῶνος καὶ ἡ ἀπάτη τοῦ πλούτου καὶ αἱ περὶ τὰ λοιπὰ ἐπιθυμίαι εἰσπορευόμεναι συμπνίγουσιν τὸν λόγον καὶ ἄκαρπος γίνεται

passages.text: Still others are like the seeds sown on good soil. They hear the word, receive it, and produce a crop—thirtyfold, sixtyfold, or a hundredfold.”
passages.sermon:
Some people are like seeds sown on good soil.
These people hear the word.
They accept the word.
They produce a crop.
Some produce thirty times what was sown.
Some produce sixty times what was sown.
Some produce a hundred times what was sown.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐκεῖνοί εἰσιν οἱ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν τὴν καλὴν σπαρέντες οἵτινες ἀκούουσιν τὸν λόγον καὶ παραδέχονται καὶ καρποφοροῦσιν ἓν τριάκοντα καὶ ἓν ἑξήκοντα καὶ ἓν ἑκατόν

passages.text: Jesus also said to them, “Does anyone bring in a lamp to put it under a basket or under a bed? Doesn’t he set it on a stand?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He asked a question.
He said, “Does anyone bring a lamp to hide it under a basket?
Does anyone put a lamp under a bed?
No one does this.
People put a lamp on a stand.
A lamp gives light when it is on a stand.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ὅτι Μήτι ἔρχεται ὁ λύχνος ἵνα ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον τεθῇ ἢ ὑπὸ τὴν κλίνην οὐχ ἵνα ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν τεθῇ

passages.text: For there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed, and nothing concealed that will not be brought to light.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He taught them about truth and revelation.
Nothing remains hidden forever.
Everything that is secret will be revealed.
Everything that is concealed will come to light.
passages.original: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν τι κρυπτὸν ἐὰν μὴ ἵνα φανερωθῇ οὐδὲ ἐγένετο ἀπόκρυφον ἀλλ’ ἵνα ἔλθῃ εἰς φανερόν

passages.text: If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the people.\r\nHe said, “If anyone has ears, he should listen.”
passages.original: Εἴ τις ἔχει ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω

passages.text: He went on to say, “Pay attention to what you hear. With the measure you use, it will be measured to you, and even more will be added to you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He told them to pay attention to what they hear.
He said, "The measure you use will be used for you."
He said, "You will receive even more than that."
passages.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Βλέπετε τί ἀκούετε ἐν ᾧ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε μετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν καὶ προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν

passages.text: For whoever has will be given more. But whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He explained a spiritual principle.
Whoever has will receive more.
Whoever does not have will lose even what he has.
God gives more to those who already possess.
God takes away from those who do not possess.
passages.original: ὃς γὰρ ἔχει δοθήσεται αὐτῷ καὶ ὃς οὐκ ἔχει καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Jesus also said, “The kingdom of God is like a man who scatters seed on the ground.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He explained the kingdom of God.
The kingdom of God is like a man.
This man scatters seed on the ground.
passages.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν Οὕτως ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ ὡς ἄνθρωπος βάλῃ τὸν σπόρον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς

passages.text: Night and day he sleeps and wakes, and the seed sprouts and grows, though he knows not how.
passages.sermon:
A man scatters seed on the ground.
He sleeps at night.
He wakes during the day.
This happens again and again.
The seed sprouts.
The seed grows.
The man does not know how the seed grows.
passages.original: καὶ καθεύδῃ καὶ ἐγείρηται νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν καὶ ὁ σπόρος βλαστᾷ καὶ μηκύνηται ὡς οὐκ οἶδεν αὐτός

passages.text: All by itself the earth produces a crop—first the stalk, then the head, then grain that ripens within.
passages.sermon:
The earth produces a crop by itself.
First, the earth brings up a stalk.
Next, the earth forms a head of grain.
Then, the earth fills the head with ripe grain.
passages.original: αὐτομάτη ἡ γῆ καρποφορεῖ πρῶτον χόρτον εἶτα στάχυν εἶτα πλήρης σῖτον ἐν τῷ στάχυϊ

passages.text: And as soon as the grain is ripe, he swings the sickle, because the harvest has come.”
passages.sermon:
A man plants seed in the ground.
The seed grows into grain.
When the grain becomes ripe, the man acts quickly.
He takes his sickle.
He cuts the grain.
He does this because the time for harvest has arrived.
passages.original: ὅταν δὲ παραδοῖ ὁ καρπός εὐθὺς ἀποστέλλει τὸ δρέπανον ὅτι παρέστηκεν ὁ θερισμός

passages.text: Then He asked, “To what can we compare the kingdom of God? With what parable shall we present it?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus wanted to explain the kingdom of God.
Jesus asked a question.
He said, “How can we compare the kingdom of God?
What parable can we use to describe it?”
passages.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν Πῶς ὁμοιώσωμεν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἢ ἐν τίνι αὐτὴν παραβολῇ θῶμεν

passages.text: It is like a mustard seed, which is the smallest of all seeds sown upon the earth.
passages.sermon: Jesus compared the kingdom of God to a mustard seed.\r\nA mustard seed is very small.\r\nIt is the smallest seed that people plant in the ground.
passages.original: ὡς κόκκῳ σινάπεως ὃς ὅταν σπαρῇ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς μικρότερον ὂν πάντων τῶν σπερμάτων τῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς

passages.text: But after it is planted, it grows to be the largest of all garden plants and puts forth great branches, so that the birds of the air nest in its shade.”
passages.sermon:
A person plants the mustard seed in the ground.
The mustard seed begins to grow.
It becomes larger than all other garden plants.
It produces large branches.
The birds of the air can rest and make nests in its shade.
passages.original: καὶ ὅταν σπαρῇ ἀναβαίνει καὶ γίνεται μεῖζον πάντων τῶν λαχάνων καὶ ποιεῖ κλάδους μεγάλους ὥστε δύνασθαι ὑπὸ τὴν σκιὰν αὐτοῦ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατασκηνοῦν

passages.text: With many such parables Jesus spoke the word to them, to the extent that they could understand.
passages.sermon: Jesus often spoke to the people using many parables.\r\nHe taught them the word of God in this way.\r\nHe used parables so they could understand as much as they were able.
passages.original: Καὶ τοιαύταις παραβολαῖς πολλαῖς ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον καθὼς ἠδύναντο ἀκούειν

passages.text: He did not tell them anything without using a parable. But privately He explained everything to His own disciples.
passages.sermon: Jesus always used parables when He spoke to the people.\r\nHe did not speak to them without a parable.\r\nBut Jesus explained everything to His own disciples in private.
passages.original: χωρὶς δὲ παραβολῆς οὐκ ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς κατ’ ἰδίαν δὲ τοῖς ἰδίοις μαθηταῖς ἐπέλυεν πάντα

passages.text: When that evening came, He said to His disciples, “Let us cross to the other side.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was with His disciples.
Evening came that day.
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Let us cross to the other side.”
passages.original: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ὀψίας γενομένης Διέλθωμεν εἰς τὸ πέραν

passages.text: After they had dismissed the crowd, they took Jesus with them, since He was already in the boat. And there were other boats with Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was already in the boat.
The disciples dismissed the crowd.
The disciples took Jesus with them in the boat.
Other boats were with Jesus.
passages.original: καὶ ἀφέντες τὸν ὄχλον παραλαμβάνουσιν αὐτὸν ὡς ἦν ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ καὶ ἄλλα πλοῖα ἦν μετ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Soon a violent windstorm came up, and the waves were breaking over the boat, so that it was being swamped.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was in the boat with His disciples.
A violent windstorm began suddenly.
Strong winds blew over the water.
Waves crashed against the boat.
Water started filling the boat.
The boat was being swamped by the waves.
passages.original: Καὶ γίνεται λαῖλαψ μεγάλη ἀνέμου καὶ τὰ κύματα ἐπέβαλλεν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον ὥστε ἤδη γεμίζεσθαι τὸ πλοῖον

passages.text: But Jesus was in the stern, sleeping on the cushion. So they woke Him and said, “Teacher, don’t You care that we are perishing?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was in the stern of the boat.
He was sleeping on a cushion.
The disciples woke Jesus.
They spoke to Him.
They said, “Teacher, do You not care that we are perishing?”
passages.original: καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν ἐν τῇ πρύμνῃ ἐπὶ τὸ προσκεφάλαιον καθεύδων καὶ ἐγείρουσιν αὐτὸν καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Διδάσκαλε οὐ μέλει σοι ὅτι ἀπολλύμεθα

passages.text: Then Jesus got up and rebuked the wind and the sea. “Silence!” He commanded. “Be still!” And the wind died down, and it was perfectly calm.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was in the boat with His disciples.
A violent windstorm was happening.
The waves were breaking over the boat.
The boat was being swamped.
Jesus got up.
He spoke to the wind.
He rebuked the wind.
He spoke to the sea.
He said, “Silence! Be still!”
The wind stopped.
The sea became perfectly calm.
passages.original: Καὶ διεγερθεὶς ἐπετίμησεν τῷ ἀνέμῳ καὶ εἶπεν τῇ θαλάσσῃ Σιώπα πεφίμωσο καὶ ἐκόπασεν ὁ ἄνεμος καὶ ἐγένετο γαλήνη μεγάλη

passages.text: “Why are you so afraid?” He asked. “Do you still have no faith?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He asked them a question.
He said, “Why are you so afraid?”
He said, “Do you still have no faith?”
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τί δειλοί ἐστε οὔπω ἔχετε πίστιν

passages.text: Overwhelmed with fear, they asked one another, “Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?”
passages.sermon:
The disciples saw what Jesus did.
They became very afraid.
They felt great fear.
They spoke to each other.
They asked, “Who is this man?”
They saw that even the wind obeyed Jesus.
They saw that the sea obeyed Jesus too.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν φόβον μέγαν καὶ ἔλεγον πρὸς ἀλλήλους Τίς ἄρα οὗτός ἐστιν ὅτι καὶ ὁ ἄνεμος καὶ ἡ θάλασσα ὑπακούει αὐτῷ
